title: API Gateways & Event-Driven Architecture
description: Explore API Gateway policies, GraphQL federation, publish-subscribe brokers, and transactional outbox patterns.

questions.question: What role does an API Gateway serve in a microservices ecosystem?
options: Acts as a single entry point handling routing, authentication, rate limiting, and protocol translation
Stores all customer payment passwords in plaintext
Compiles backend source code upon every incoming user request
Replaces all frontend browser rendering logic

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of Event-Driven Architecture (EDA)?
options: Decouples service producers and consumers for independent scalability and asynchronous processing
Requires every microservice to share a single monolithic SQL database
Eliminates the need for API documentation
Forces synchronous HTTP blocking across all service calls

questions.question: What does the 'Transactional Outbox Pattern' guarantee?
options: Reliable dual-writes: database updates and outgoing events are saved in the same local transaction before publishing to the broker
Zero-latency email dispatch across SMTP relays
Real-time websocket connections to mobile devices without reconnects
Instant rollback of user bank transfers upon UI close

questions.question: What problem does GraphQL solve compared to traditional REST endpoints?
options: Prevents over-fetching and under-fetching by allowing clients to request precisely the data fields they need in a single query
Eliminates the need for SSL/TLS encryption
Guarantees that database queries run without any indexes
Replaces the HTTP protocol with Bluetooth connections

questions.question: Why is 'Idempotency' critical when consuming distributed event messages?
options: It ensures that receiving duplicate event deliveries produces the exact same outcome without duplicate side-effects
It compresses message size by 90%
It guarantees messages are always received in sub-millisecond time
It converts XML payloads into JSON format automatically
